# Geographic Advanced {.center}

## Topics Covered

- Spatial interpolation (IDW; kriging in the GIS track)
- Cartograms (area distortion)
- Spatial autocorrelation
- Hexagon tile maps
- Access: distance bands

Goal: Advanced spatial analysis

## Setup

Data: a synthetic district of 79 blocks with dengue rates, and 30 health facilities
(`data/gis/`, built by `gis/make_gis_data.R`; the same data as the GIS track).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse); library(sf)
blocks <- st_read("../../data/gis/district_blocks.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(32644)                                   # UTM zone 44N: metres, for distances and areas
fac <- read_csv("../../data/gis/facilities.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("easting_m", "northing_m"), crs = 32644)
```
:::


## Spatial Interpolation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(gstat)
centres <- st_centroid(blocks)
grid <- st_make_grid(blocks, cellsize = 500, what = "centers") |> st_as_sf() |>
  st_filter(st_union(blocks))                            # 500 m grid inside the district
idw_fit <- idw(dengue_per_100k ~ 1, centres, newdata = grid, idp = 2, debug.level = 0)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = idw_fit, aes(colour = var1.pred), size = 0.6, shape = 15) +
  geom_sf(data = blocks, fill = NA, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Dengue\nper 100k") +
  labs(title = "Inverse distance weighting from block centres") +
  theme_void()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](3.6_geographic_advanced_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){fig-alt='Smooth surface of dengue incidence per 100,000 estimated by inverse distance weighting from the 79 block centres, with block outlines on top.' width=960}
:::
:::


Estimates values **between** observations. Kriging does the same with a fitted variogram and gives a standard error
for each estimate (GIS track).

## Cartogram


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(cartogram)
carto <- cartogram_cont(blocks, "population", itermax = 8)
ggplot(carto) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = dengue_per_100k), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Dengue\nper 100k") +
  labs(title = "Cartogram: block area proportional to population") +
  theme_void()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](3.6_geographic_advanced_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-alt='Cartogram of the district in which each block\'s area is distorted to be proportional to its population, shaded by dengue incidence.' width=960}
:::
:::


Large empty blocks shrink and crowded ones grow, so the map shows **where the people are**, not where the land is.

## Spatial Autocorrelation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(spdep)
nb <- poly2nb(blocks)                                   # blocks that share a border
lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W")
moran_result <- moran.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw)
moran.plot(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, labels = FALSE, pch = 19,
           xlab = "Dengue per 100k", ylab = "Neighbours' average",
           main = sprintf("Moran's I = %.2f, p = %.3g", moran_result$estimate[1], moran_result$p.value))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](3.6_geographic_advanced_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){fig-alt='Moran scatter plot of dengue incidence in each block against the average incidence of its neighbours, with a positive slope.' width=960}
:::
:::


A positive slope (Moran's I > 0) means high-incidence blocks sit next to high-incidence blocks.

## Hexagon Tile Map


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(geogrid)
blocks_wgs <- st_transform(blocks, 4326)
hex_grid <- calculate_grid(shape = blocks_wgs, grid_type = "hexagonal", seed = 3)
hex_data <- assign_polygons(blocks_wgs, hex_grid)
ggplot(hex_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = dengue_per_100k), colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Dengue\nper 100k") +
  labs(title = "Every block the same size") +
  theme_void()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](3.6_geographic_advanced_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-alt='The 79 blocks redrawn as equal-sized hexagons placed close to their real positions, shaded by dengue incidence.' width=960}
:::
:::


Small blocks are as visible as large ones; the price is distorted positions and shapes.

## Access: Distance Bands


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
phc <- fac |> filter(type %in% c("PHC", "CHC"))
bands <- map_dfr(c(10, 5, 2), \(km) st_sf(km = km, geometry = st_union(st_buffer(phc, km * 1000)))) |>
  st_intersection(st_union(blocks))
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bands, aes(fill = factor(km, levels = c(2, 5, 10))), colour = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = blocks, fill = NA, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = phc, aes(shape = type), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "YlGnBu", direction = -1, name = "Within (km)") +
  labs(title = "Straight-line distance to a PHC or CHC", shape = NULL) +
  theme_void()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](3.6_geographic_advanced_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-alt='District map with shaded bands of 2, 5 and 10 kilometres around the primary and community health centres, and the facilities as points.' width=960}
:::
:::


Straight-line bands are a first look. **Isochrones** (travel time by road, e.g. `osrm::osrmIsochrone()`)
are better, but need a routing server and road data.

## Summary

**Advanced geographic techniques:**

1. Spatial interpolation - estimate unmeasured locations
2. Cartograms - size by variable
3. Spatial autocorrelation - test clustering
4. Hexagon tile maps - equal area representation
5. Distance bands - accessibility (isochrones need a routing server)

**Next:** Dashboards Advanced

  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
